ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing rules are principally contained in Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-1 et seq. and R561-1 et seq., including customer due diligence, beneficial-owner identification, enhanced measures, suspicious-transaction reporting, recordkeeping, and sanctions-screening obligations. Beneficial-owner identification and filing for legal entities are governed principally by Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-46 et seq., Articles R561-1 et seq., and Code de commerce provisions concerning the Registre national des entreprises. The beneficial-owner filing framework was introduced and supplemented by Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 and Décret n° 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017, as amended. The commercial registration and filing framework is also governed by Code de commerce, including Articles L123-1 et seq. and R123-1 et seq. Access to beneficial-owner information is restricted following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment in Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 and subsequent French implementation measures.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all managers, shareholders, authorized signatories, UBOs, controllers, and relevant counterparties before incorporation and periodically thereafter against United Nations sanctions lists, European Union sanctions regulations, French national sanctions measures and registers, and commercially reliable PEP, adverse-media, and sanctions databases. OFAC screening is not generally a standalone mandatory French-law requirement but is required where there is a United States nexus, US-dollar clearing, US persons, US technology, or contractual exposure, and is a prudent enhanced-control measure. Resolve name matches using date of birth, nationality, address, identifiers, and documentary evidence. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, relatives and close associates, opaque ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, nominee arrangements, unexplained wealth, and unusual payment flows. File a suspicious transaction report with TRACFIN where statutory suspicion exists; do not disclose the filing to the customer. Maintain screening records and identification evidence for the statutory retention period, generally five years after the relationship ends or the transaction is completed, subject to applicable extensions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with registration data recorded in the Registre national des entreprises and, where applicable, the Registre du commerce et des sociétés
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be stated in the articles of association and filing documents. French law does not generally require a SARL name to be exclusively in French or in French script, but the name must be legally valid, sufficiently distinctive, non-misleading, and compatible with public order. A French-language corporate designation identifying the legal form, such as Société à responsabilité limitée or SARL, must be used in the statutory and commercial documentation as applicable. Foreign words, Latin characters, and transliterations are generally permitted, subject to registry, trademark, prior-rights, public-order, and regulated-activity restrictions. The name must be checked against existing company names, trademarks, trade names, domain names, and protected geographical or institutional designations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Investissement or financial-services terms implying a regulated activity
École or academic terms implying an accredited institution
État, République, France, Ministère, Préfecture, or similar official-state designations where use could create confusion or imply public authority
Any term suggesting a regulated profession, public authority, licensed financial activity, or official institutional status without the required authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a general statutory company-name reservation procedure with a universal 30-day reservation period. Name clearance is an availability and prior-rights exercise rather than a binding reservation. Before filing, conduct searches through INPI, the Registre national des entreprises, trademark databases, domain-name databases, and relevant commercial databases. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the filing, identify whether the objection concerns legal form, misleading wording, regulated terminology, prior rights, public order, incomplete documents, or technical filing defects. Correct and resubmit through the Guichet unique where permitted. Request written reasons and preserve the filing record. A registry or formalities decision may be challenged through the competent commercial court or other legally competent court, depending on the decision and procedural basis; trademark disputes may require proceedings before the competent judicial court or an opposition before INPI. There is no general administrative appeal that guarantees acceptance of a rejected company name. A revised name is ordinarily the fastest risk-control solution.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SARL must have a registered office in France. Commercial domiciliation is generally permissible under Code de commerce, including Article L123-11-1 and related provisions, if provided by an authorized domiciliation business under a compliant domiciliation agreement and if the company can receive legal and administrative notices. A manager may, subject to statutory conditions and applicable lease or condominium restrictions, use a personal residence for registered-office purposes for the permitted period. A virtual office is not sufficient by itself to establish operational substance, tax residence, transfer-pricing support, employment presence, or eligibility for regulated or sector-specific activities. For a developer-infrastructure, database, and API-monitoring cloud business with no identified statutory license, a compliant domiciliation address may be accepted for incorporation, but a bank, payment institution, tax authority, auditor, or AML provider may require evidence of actual management, personnel, contracts, servers or hosting arrangements, accounting records, and customer activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable official nationwide probability is published. For a low-risk standard software and cloud activity, with complete filings, transparent ownership, a regulated domiciliation provider, and consistent tax and banking records, the estimated risk of an unannounced physical inspection during pre-incorporation is low, approximately 1% to 3% on a planning basis; this is an operational estimate, not a statutory rate. The risk increases materially where the address is a mass-use virtual office, mail is undeliverable, UBO information is inconsistent, tax filings are absent, activity differs from the declared purpose, payment flows are unusual, or the company presents heightened AML, sanctions, employment, consumer, cybersecurity, or VAT indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 through L.223-53 and R.223-1 through R.223-26, governing the formation, management, capital, and dissolution of a Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS), maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; electronic filing intake is through the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Unified incorporation declaration file (dossier unique d'immatriculation) comprising the M0 declaration form and statutory annexes, submitted on the INPI Guichet Unique; the constitution is evidenced by the RCS Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a SARL; the articles may set capital at €1. For cash contributions, at least 20% of each subscriber's contribution must be paid up at incorporation, and the balance must be settled within five years. The paid-up amount must be deposited in a blocked account with a bank or notary, or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and released to the company only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a properly convened meeting of the founding shareholders, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted: 1. The draft articles of association for a private limited liability company (SARL) are approved as presented. 2. The entire share capital set forth in the articles, the paid-up portion of which has been deposited with the designated depository bank, is subscribed and allotted to the founding shareholders. 3. The registered office is fixed at 10 Rue de la Boétie, 75008 Paris, and the company is authorized to file for RCS registration. 4. The first general manager (gérant) is appointed with full corporate and bank-signing authority. 5. All filings, publication notices and banking formalities necessary for incorporation are ratified. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name verification and legal announcement preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI data directory and Registre du commerce et des sociétés database; support d'annonces légales approved by the commercial court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search available corporate names and trademarks on data.inpi.fr to avoid identical or confusing designations. Draft the corporate denomination, corporate purpose, registered office address, share classes, allocation of profits, and governance provisions in the articles. Prepare the mandatory legal announcement text for publication in an authorized legal gazette covering the jurisdiction of the company's registered office.
required_dossiers: Name availability search result from the INPI/RCS database
Draft articles of association
Draft legal announcement text for constitution of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an identical or confusingly similar name is found, amend the corporate denomination, update the draft articles, and republish the legal announcement; there is no a priori acquiescence procedure at the RCS level.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription, allocation and escrow deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated blocked account in the name of the company being formed or engage a notary as depositary. Each cash subscriber must pay at least 20% of the nominal cash contribution subscribed. The depositary will issue the certificate of deposit (certificat du dépositaire des fonds), which is a mandatory annex to the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association showing share allocation
Identity documents of founding shareholders
Bank or notary capital deposit mandate
Application for release of blocked funds upon Kbis issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the blocker account, retain a notary as depositary under Article L.223-7 of the Code de commerce or use the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; no capital contribution may be treated as paid-up without a valid depositary certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of articles and first formal governance acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and the appointed gérant; optional notary if real-property contributions are made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all shareholders sign the final articles of association and the share subscription schedule. Obtain the written consent of the nominated gérant, the declaration of non-conviction, and the first board resolution ratifying incorporation steps. Initial each page and ensure formal signatures are reconciled with identity documents.
required_dossiers: Signed final articles of association
Share subscription and capital allocation schedule
Written acceptance of office by the appointed gérant
Declaration of non-conviction for each manager and shareholder where applicable
Pro-forma first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry detects a legal defect in the articles, all shareholders must sign an avenant or a corrective resolution to cure the defect and refile the amended articles with the same filing package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of electronic incorporation dossier to INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique; forwarding to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr using FranceConnect+ or an approved electronic identity. Select 'immatriculation d'une société' and complete the M0 declaration. Upload all statutory annexes in PDF, pay the prescribed greffe fee, and submit. The INPI transfers the file to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, which verifies legal regularity and effects registration.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 declaration form
Signed articles of association
Certificate of capital deposit from bank or notary
Attestation of legal announcement publication
Proof of occupation or domiciliation of the registered office
Copy of valid national ID or passport of each shareholder and manager
Declaration of beneficial owner
Declaration of non-conviction for each manager
Power of attorney if a filing agent is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or Greffe issues a request for complementary information or rectification, respond through the same portal within the statutory 15-day deadline; failure to cure leads to closure of the file and a new submission is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, Kbis issuance and automatic INSEE/DGFiP follow-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE assigns SIREN/SIRET and DGFiP issues French tax identifiers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Greffe validates legal compliance, the company is registered in the RCS and receives the official Kbis extract. The SIREN/SIRET numbers are automatically created by INSEE, and the DGFiP generates the French VAT and corporate income tax identifiers. The blocked capital is then released to the company's operational bank account.
required_dossiers: No additional documents are required for this step; the registry acts on the completed incorporation file
Bank release instruction referencing the new Kbis extract and SIREN number
Original capital deposit certificate returned to the depositary for release
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance is delayed or SIREN/VAT data is incorrect, file a request for rectification with the Greffe; INSEE and DGFiP must correct the automatic notifications ex officio.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 is a non-industrial software and cloud service activity; no industrial establishment permit or dedicated licensing board is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license or manufacturing permit is required for the DevTools cloud infrastructure, database and API monitoring service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement) and the municipal environmental services as applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the business is an office-based software and data-service activity without physical production works, installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE), or IOTA; no environmental impact assessment is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous industrial waste streams. General compliance with EU waste and circular economy requirements applies, including Directive (EU) 2019/904 for single-use plastics, WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU for e-waste disposal, and municipal ordinary-waste collection standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense license applies to this office-based software activity. The leased premises must possess a valid building fire safety certificate under the Code du travail, meet structural load requirements for IT equipment, and pass the obligatory occupational health and workplace electrical safety inspection before employee deployment. Fire prevention, evacuation plans, and first-aid equipment must be maintained as a function of staff headcount.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) or Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) for non-resident businesses. Principal online portal: impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and business registration data are filed through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); the INPI process allocates the SIREN and SIRET identifiers, while DGFiP administers tax registration and VAT identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is registered through the INPI Guichet unique. Following registration, the company receives a SIREN identifier for the legal entity and a SIRET identifier for each establishment. The DGFiP assigns or confirms the corporate tax account and the French VAT identification number, generally formatted as FR followed by a two-digit VAT key and the nine-digit SIREN. The company must open and maintain its professional account on impots.gouv.fr, select the applicable corporate income tax and VAT obligations, and provide constitutional documents, registered-office evidence, identity and authority documents for the legal representative, bank details, and business-activity information when requested. A foreign entity without a French establishment that is required to register for French VAT applies to the SIEE and submits evidence of foreign establishment, commercial activity, French taxable transactions, representative authority, and VAT status in its home jurisdiction. An EU-established business generally does not need a French fiscal representative; a non-EU business normally requires a French fiscal representative for VAT compliance unless an applicable statutory exemption applies. VAT registration is not automatically required where a business validly uses the French VAT franchise regime or where the reverse charge applies, but cross-border transactions may create registration or reporting obligations independently of the domestic turnover threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is normally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Eligible SARLs may elect for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu), generally subject to statutory conditions, including qualifying ownership and activity requirements and a maximum election period of five financial years for the ordinary temporary regime. A family SARL may elect for income-tax treatment without the ordinary five-year limitation if the statutory family-company conditions are satisfied. France has no general US-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing ATAD 2 can deny deductions, require inclusion, or otherwise neutralize mismatches involving hybrid entities, instruments, or permanent establishments; these rules are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), supplemented by EU place-of-supply, intra-Community, customs, and reverse-charge rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the French domestic VAT franchise regime applicable to services and non-commercial professional activities, the principal turnover threshold is EUR 37,500 for the preceding calendar year, with a current-year tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250, subject to statutory exclusions, sector-specific rules, and legislative changes. The thresholds do not eliminate VAT registration or reporting obligations for transactions for which VAT is due under a special place-of-supply rule, including certain cross-border B2B services. The principal goods threshold is EUR 85,000 for the preceding year, with a current-year tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500. A business may voluntarily opt for VAT liability and may be required to register despite turnover below a franchise threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved Partner Dematerialization Platforms (Plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, or PDPs). From 1 September 2026, all French-established businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; large businesses and entities in the intermediate-size category generally become subject to mandatory issuance from that date. Small and medium-sized businesses and micro-enterprises generally become subject to mandatory issuance from 1 September 2027. The regime covers domestic B2B transactions subject to French VAT and requires e-reporting for specified cross-border and business-to-consumer transactions. Invoices must use required structured or structured-plus-image formats and contain mandatory tax data. France does not generally operate a universal pre-issuance real-time clearance system requiring each invoice to receive a tax-authority approval stamp; transmission occurs through the approved platform architecture, with data forwarded to DGFiP. Public-sector invoicing continues to use the Chorus Pro framework where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption at the French seller level, functionally equivalent to zero-rating, where the exporter can prove that the goods left the EU customs territory and satisfy the applicable export and customs conditions. Required evidence normally includes the electronic export declaration, Movement Reference Number (MRN), customs exit confirmation, transport documentation, commercial invoice, and proof linking the goods to the export transaction. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer has a valid VAT identification number in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier retains the required transport and customer-status evidence. Services supplied to a business established outside France are generally governed by the B2B place-of-supply rule and may be outside the scope of French VAT rather than technically zero-rated; the supplier must retain customer-location, contractual, invoicing, and payment evidence. Digital and cloud services require analysis of customer status, establishment, place of supply, and any specific electronically supplied-services rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent proof that the goods exited the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, VAT treatment, and transaction reference
Transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or carrier delivery evidence
Packing list and, where relevant, export authorization, preference, or origin documentation
Evidence linking the customs export record and transport evidence to the relevant sales invoice
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification validation and transport evidence to the destination Member State
For offshore B2B services: customer establishment and business-status evidence, contract, service records, invoice, and evidence supporting the applicable place-of-supply treatment
Bank payment or receivable records where relevant to audit substantiation; an inward-remittance certificate is not a generally mandatory French export-VAT document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. French VAT exemption or zero-rating must be supported by contemporaneous evidence of the applicable export, intra-Community, or place-of-supply conditions. DGFiP may assess unpaid VAT retrospectively, together with late-payment interest and tax penalties, where the exemption is unsupported, incorrectly applied, or connected with fraudulent conduct. The standard penalty framework may include a 5% penalty for certain late or deficient VAT payment situations, a 40% penalty for deliberate failure, an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, and potentially a 100% penalty in cases involving opposition to a tax audit, subject to statutory conditions and procedural rights. Input VAT refunds may be denied or clawed back, and previously claimed deductions may be reassessed. Customs infringements can additionally result in recovery of duties and taxes, customs penalties, seizure, and criminal or administrative sanctions. Intentional false invoicing, fabricated export evidence, or VAT fraud may trigger criminal proceedings and enhanced sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) — Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor; EU Treaty freedom of capital movement under TFEU Articles 63-65; ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority) supervises banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; France maintains no residual exchange-control authorization for current or capital transactions. Current account convertibility is unrestricted, and capital account transactions (forming an SARL, capital contributions, dividend distributions, loan repayments, intercompany treasury flows) are liberalized. Profit remittance constraints are tax-driven, not FX-driven: dividends paid by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders are subject to French withholding tax of 25% (or reduced tax-treaty rate upon presentation of a French tax residence certificate), but the remittance itself is free. Cross-border flows above de minimis thresholds are subject to statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France, executed by the resident payment institution on behalf of the company; no prior approval is needed for a non-resident to own shares in the SARL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or compulsory conversion of export receipts exists for French residents. Export proceeds invoiced in foreign currency may be retained in foreign-currency current accounts at French authorized intermediaries. Under Articles L151-1 to L151-4 and R151-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier, resident exporters must channel export receivables through an authorized French bank (rapatriement) within the payment terms agreed in the commercial contract (subject to French/EU statutory payment deadlines applicable to B2B trade), and provide the intermediary with sufficient information (invoice, nature of transaction, counterparty) to enable the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistics. There is no fixed statutory conversion ratio or time limit other than contractual terms. Penalties apply only for deliberate non-reporting or use of unauthorized foreign accounts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for EEA-authorized EMIs (Qonto, Revolut Business, Wise Business) operating under PSD2 passporting into France; LOW for offshore digital EMIs and US-based platforms such as Mercury. A French SARL cannot onboard with Mercury without a distinct US subsidiary/Delaware entity because Mercury targets US LLCs and does not hold a French/EEA EMI license; US ACH rails (target_payment_rails 'Mercury_ACH') are therefore only relevant through a US intermediate vehicle. Stripe Billing can be retained directly by the French entity, settling USD/EUR into the French bank account. Legal constraints: non-EEA EMI accounts are permissible as ancillary clearing accounts but do not satisfy the French rapatriement channel and all cross-border movements must still be notified to the Banque de France; accordingly, the principal treasury and clearing relationship must remain with a French-licensed credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banking law (Code monétaire et financier Article L561-5 et seq. and ACPR recommendations) does not formally require a physical appearance for account opening; however, tier-1 banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale) impose in-practice a single on-site or high-grade certified video interview for non-resident directors/UBOs, and require eIDAS-qualified electronic signature or apostilled wet signatures for the SARL's Kbis, statuts, gérant designation and UBO declaration. For EU-resident directors, remote video KYC with notarized board minutes is generally accepted; for non-EU directors, a physical visit to the branch or to the French consulate for notarized/legalized documents will be required. A director acting as représentant légal with French residency smoothens onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident majority UBO chain or multi-layer foreign parent holding; failure to document the source of wealth and control chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract (less than 3 months); SARL statuts and gérant appointment resolution; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) declaration; group organizational chart; apostilled/certified certificates of incorporation and director registers of each foreign parent; passport copies of UBOs (notarized/apostilled); bank references from the ultimate parent's principal bank; narrative of source of funds for the initial capital deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: DevOps/API monitoring business with automated Stripe billing, open-source components, or donation-based inflows creating unexplained payment volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business model memorandum describing ISIC 6201 activities (developer infrastructure, database and API monitoring cloud); Stripe Billing merchant agreement and settlement volume reports; specimen invoices and three benchmark customer contracts; cloud vendor contracts (AWS/Azure/GCP); open-source license compliance register; statement that no virtual currencies are accepted; revenue recognition policy under IFRS/French GAAP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate USD inbound flows with requests for rapid onward transfers to third-country shareholders (layering/straw-man red flag).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SaaS subscription agreements; API usage monitoring logs and delivery evidence; consolidated invoices reconciled to Stripe payouts; intercompany treasury/TP policy (fichier des prix de transfert) with OECD-compliant benchmarking; beneficiary attribution analysis; FX hedging documentation (forward contracts proving commercial motive); approval chain in the SARL treasury policy and internal controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient equity relative to expected turnover ('shell company' profile) or inability to provide physical substance evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Attestation de dépôt des fonds from the receiving bank; detailed 3-year financial projections; payroll and French social-security registrations; office lease; SIRET/SIRENE registration with NAF 6201Z; insurance certificates (RC Pro); capital allocation/capex plan for the monitoring infrastructure; external accountant letter confirming substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The shareholder (EU or offshore) must initiate a SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022) for EUR or SWIFT MT103 for USD into the SARL's temporary capital-deposit account held at a French Tier-1 bank. The wire must cite the legal basis and purpose in field 70 of the MT103/remittance information of the pain.001 (e.g., 'Capital subscription — apport en numéraire', with a Banque de France balance-of-payments reason-code for inward direct investment as instructed by the receiving bank). Required verification bundle: executed share-subscription resolution, updated list of subscribers, nationality and residence of each contributing shareholder, ultimate beneficial-owner declaration (RBE), proof of origin of funds (six months bank statements), and, when relevant, French FDI declaration if the non-EU investor acquires control (generally not triggered for a minority SARL shareholding, but verified). The bank issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds only after irrevocable blocking of funds; release to the operative account occurs upon registration of the company (Kbis issuance). Cash or third-party funding is prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EEA/EU suppliers and cloud providers: SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) cleared through TARGET2/STEP2; for USD or non-EEA destinations: SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details (field 57A/59), purpose-code and supporting invoice (delivery certificates if hardware used). Commercial documentary credits (UCP600) are reserved for larger infrastructure procurements or suppliers in restricted jurisdictions and will be issued by the French bank as issuing bank or confirmed by a correspondent bank; given the low-risk SaaS infrastructure profile, open-account MT103/CSM settlement is the standard rail. In addition, BNP Paribas/Société Générale API cash-management channels allow real-time multi-bank liquidity sweeping between the EUR operational account, USD shadow account and FX forward settlements; all outbound EBICS/API transactions are screened against French AML sanctions, OFAC/EU lists and transfer-pricing benchmarks before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (change à terme) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF, maturity up to 12-24 months, with collateral/deposit margin agreed under the bank's master agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid/restricted currencies (e.g., INR, offshore CNH, emerging-market currencies) executed only through the bank's regulated FX desk where physical delivery is legally impossible; documentation under FBF/ISDA 2002 with net settlement

Cross-currency swaps (CIRS/CCS) converting USD or other debt/cash flows into EUR to cover long-dated treasury mismatches, permitted under EMIR trade-reporting thresholds as a non-financial counterparty and under the SARL's board-approved hedging policy
EUR/USD spot execution (FX swap of two-leg same-day/next-day) for working capital conversion, compliant with MiFID II suitability/professional-client classification
